I'll think through my year the way I always do — start from what I did last year and change only what I have reason to change.

**My thinking:**

I've farmed these 5 mu for 25 years. Wheat goes in October, maize follows in June after I cut the wheat. That's how everyone around here does it in Quzhou.

For **wheat seed**, I buy improved variety from the seed shop in town — Jimai 22 or whatever my neighbor Old Wang bought last year if his field looked good. I don't save my own seed for wheat, germination gets bad. For **maize**, I buy hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or Denghai. Hybrid costs more but the ears are full and even. No one around here plants old varieties anymore.

For **wheat fertilizer**, I use about one and a half bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu as base (around 60 kg), then topdress urea at green-up in spring, about half a bag per mu (25 kg). That gives me around 20 kg of nitrogen per mu. I know this is maybe a bit more than what the extension man said at the village meeting, but I'd rather the wheat be a little dark green than risk yellow patches. A bag of fertilizer is 100 yuan; a bad wheat crop is 400 yuan loss per mu. I don't gamble on fertilizer.

For **maize**, I put one bag of compound (50 kg) at planting, then topdress 20-25 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. About 19 kg N. Maize is hungrier in July when it's growing fast.

**Irrigation** — I have a well so water isn't the worry, only the electricity bill. Wheat: I water at winter before freeze, again at green-up/jointing, and once at heading — three times. Maize: summer rain covers most of it, but I usually water once at planting and once at tasseling — two times. If it's a dry year I add one more.

**Pesticide**: wheat gets herbicide in spring (one spray) and aphid/scab spray at heading (one spray) — 2 times. Maize: one spray for armyworm/borer, sometimes one more — 2 times.

**Tillage**: wheat I rotary till after maize stubble — it mixes the residue. Maize I direct-seed into wheat stubble, no-till, saves time and diesel since my wife and I do it ourselves and I also work a bit off-season.

**Yield expectation**: wheat around 450 kg/mu, maize around 500 kg/mu. That's what my field gives me in a normal year.
